notes:
- The same title opens the same page on every tab: the Library, the Profile and a studio page shared four separate detail stores, so a title could arrive as two different pages and a show the Library had already loaded was fetched again from a profile. One store now serves them all - same synopsis, cast, specs and My Entry tab - and the profile's pinned favourites carry their media type, so a pinned manga no longer opens the anime that shares its number or opens with no data at all.
- Pinned characters and staff open in the app: the Favourite Characters and Favourite Staff rows used to hand the tap to the AniList website. They now open the same in-app profile sheet a title's cast row does, with the browser only as the fallback when there is no session to fetch with.
- The Info page counts down once: the progress card no longer prints "airs in in 3d", a manga says "Chapter 12 publishes in 3d" instead of airing episodes, and a title without a progress card gets a "Next episode" or "Next chapter" line in the specs card.
- The quick-add hold has a shape, not just a colour: the control rounds from a rounded rectangle into a capsule as the hold fills toward Currently Watching and springs back on release, and the app's primary button becomes a capsule while pressed and while a request is in flight.
- Long Info rows scroll, and copying says so: the sheet behind a meta row's "..." scrolls, its chevron points down, and copying a title turns the icon into a check and tints the row instead of leaving the reader guessing.
- The joke toast rises instead of falling: it is anchored to the bottom of the screen and used to animate in from above, so the one surface meant to feel like the app raising a remark read as the bar dropping it. It now rises from the bar, grows out of its own bottom edge, wears the app's sparkle instead of the update-available glyph, sits a little higher off a busy page, and is announced to a screen reader.
- The empty state stops breathing in the background: the morphing orb drew one static shape while the app was not on screen instead of spending frames on a page nobody was looking at.
- Typing in the search box no longer repaints the whole app: the viewer and the home-screen widget inputs are derived, and the widget sync runs in its own scope, so a keystroke redraws only what actually moved.
